data: This course aims to introduce students to Translation Studies (TS), by engaging with specific questions central to the domain. These questions revolve around the concept of equivalence, including issues of equivalence at various levels of language and text; they relate to challenges specific to non-literary and literary translations. At the same time, this course exposes students to various theoretical perspectives on translation in its interactions with culture. Beginning with a broad outline of the scope, history and central issues of TS, this course goes on to discuss various levels of equivalence. It begins with a focus on non-literary translation, and, thereafter, opens up to challenges specific to literary translation. Beginning with a close-up view in order to engage with these ‘building blocks’ of translation, it then goes on to view the process of translation from its place within culture and addresses issues that flow from it. Finally, it brings up some philosophical perspectives on translation. Thus, the course aims to give a comprehensive view of the act of translation and of issues concerning the domain of TS.
